item.title: 20 foreign nationals detained in the Kuyavian-Pomeranian region: return decisions and entry bans from 6 months to 2 years
item.description:
The Border Guard (Straz Graniczna) and the Police checked selected addresses in Gniewkowo and Ciechocinek. 28 people were identified and 20 foreign nationals detained — 18 citizens of Colombia plus citizens of Georgia and Tajikistan. Grounds: no valid visa or residence document, exceeding the permitted short-stay period, or no documented means of support. All received return decisions with bans on re-entering Poland and the Schengen area for 6 months to 2 years. The action followed a 30 July check at a production plant in the Inowroclaw district. Practical point: inspections increasingly move from the workplace to home addresses, and undocumented means of support is on its own a ground for a return decision. An appeal is available within the statutory deadline stated in the delivered decision.

item.title: UDSC: issuing or replacing a residence card now takes over 2 months — do not apply earlier than 2 months before your document expires
item.description:
On 10 August 2026 the Office for Foreigners (Urzad do Spraw Cudzoziemcow, UDSC) announced that, due to a sharp rise in applications, processing of further applications to issue or replace the residence card (karta pobytu) and the Geneva travel document now exceeds 2 months. The Office asks that applications not be filed earlier than 2 months before the current document expires — those filed too early are to be left without examination. UDSC will announce any changes separately. Note: the notice concerns issuing or replacing the document itself, not the deadline for deciding the residence case; the actual waiting time is worth confirming with the authority handling the case.

item.title: MSWiA: 69,000 work permits in the first half of 2026 — down by 75,000 year on year
item.description:
According to the Ministry of the Interior and Administration (Ministerstwo Spraw Wewnetrznych i Administracji, MSWiA), 69,000 work permits were issued to foreign nationals in the first half of 2026, against 144,000 in the same period of 2025 (a fall of about 52 percent) and 173,000 in the first half of 2024. The ministry links the change to new rules, digitalisation of the procedure and fewer sham applications. MSWiA notes the data are not final and are still being verified. For employers this means stricter scrutiny of applications and less tolerance for proceedings without a genuine staffing need; for foreign nationals, careful documentation. The number of permits is not the same as the number of foreign nationals working in Poland, as some work on other grounds. Secondary data — to be verified in the MSWiA announcement.

item.title: UDSC confirms: temporary protection for displaced persons from Ukraine extended to 4 March 2028
item.description:
The Office for Foreigners (Urzad do Spraw Cudzoziemcow, UDSC) confirmed that on 5 August 2026 Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1912 of 30 July 2026 entered into force, extending the temporary protection introduced by Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/382. Protection for displaced persons from Ukraine has been extended by one year, to 4 March 2028. At the same time, temporary protection is now granted only to persons who have fulfilled their military obligations in Ukraine (on presentation, where applicable, of appropriate proof); this applies from 31 July 2026. The military-obligation restriction does not apply to persons who benefited from temporary protection in a given Member State before and on 30 July 2026 and who continuously retain protected status there. Details and the application of the new condition should be confirmed in the UDSC announcement and in the text of the Council decision.
Source: Urząd do Spraw Cudzoziemców More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: UDSC: temporary protection certificates expire at the end of 4 March 2027
item.description:
The Office for Foreigners (Urzad do Spraw Cudzoziemcow, UDSC) recalls that since 5 March 2026 the Head of the Office no longer issues certificates confirming temporary protection — confirmation is now a PESEL number with UKR status and an electronic document in the mObywatel app. Certificates issued before 5 March 2026 expire at the end of 4 March 2027. While they remain valid, holders may apply for a PESEL number with UKR status without leaving Poland; once granted, the previous certificate is annulled. Holders retain, among other things, free access to the labour market, while the entity entrusting the work must notify the district labour office within 7 days (via praca.gov.pl) — except for work started before 5 March 2026. Basis: the Act of 23 January 2026 (Dz.U. poz. 203) and the Act on granting protection to foreigners (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 862). Details should be confirmed in the UDSC announcement.

item.title: Refund of the stamp duty on a temporary residence application — who is entitled and when. New COSC guide
item.description:
Since 5 March 2026 the stamp duty on a residence application is no longer refunded when the decision is negative or the proceedings are discontinued. The exceptions were introduced by the phase-out act of 23 January 2026 (Dz. U. poz. 203) and consist of the new art. 77d, 87a, 113c, 120c, 207b and 223a ustawy o cudzoziemcach, which exclude the rule in art. 9 ust. 1 pkt 2 ustawy o oplacie skarbowej. What counts is the filing date, not the decision date: applications filed before 5 March 2026 are settled under the old rules. The guide explains how the new exception relates to the general refund rule, why withdrawing an application is no longer a way to get the money back, how a refund differs from an overpayment, where and by when to apply (the tax authority whose account received the payment; five years from the end of the year of payment) and how leaving an application without examination fits in.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: The authority says it sent the summons. Who must prove delivery — new COSC guide
item.description:
The authority logged that a summons was sent, you received nothing, and the file holds neither a return receipt nor the returned envelope with delivery notes. The guide explains why that envelope can matter more than the letter itself. Deadlines in a residence case run from effective delivery, not from printing a letter or an SMS from the system. The burden of proving delivery rests on the authority, since it derives the legal effect from it. We cover substitute delivery and the delivery fiction under art. 44 k.p.a., the three different deadlines that meet here (art. 64 § 2 k.p.a., art. 106 ust. 2a and art. 112a ust. 2 ustawy o cudzoziemcach), the right to inspect the file under art. 73 k.p.a. and six steps worth taking before the case is closed. We add systemic context: findings of the NIK audit, statements by the Ombudsman (RPO), and art. 100c and 100d of the assistance act, which excluded complaints about excessive length in residence cases.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: A summons that never arrived. A nurse from Turkey has waited two and a half years for a residence card in Warsaw
item.description:
Gazeta Wyborcza reported the case of Arzu, a nurse from Turkey working in a Warsaw clinic. She arrived on 18 December 2023 and on 15 February 2024, two days before her visa expired, filed a temporary residence application with the Mazowieckie Voivode. On 2 August 2024 she received an SMS that a summons to remedy formal defects had been issued and would be posted. According to the report the letter never reached her, and the file holds no envelope confirming dispatch. The Voivode has twice refused her residence. Why the envelope matters: a summons to remedy formal defects is issued under art. 64 § 2 k.p.a. (at least 7 days), a summons to produce documents under art. 106 ust. 2a ustawy o cudzoziemcach (at least 14 days), and in both cases the effect arises only on effective delivery, which the authority must document. An SMS from the system only reports that a letter was issued. Under art. 112a ust. 2 ustawy o cudzoziemcach the 60-day deadline starts only from the last of the required events. Context: the Ombudsman's general statements (ref. XI.541.31.2021) and a NIK audit which found 60 percent of examined cases handled in breach of the rules, with the longest processing time at 2,700 days. Note: the individual case is reported solely after Gazeta Wyborcza; we have not seen the case file and have not verified the parties' claims.
Source: Gazeta Wyborcza Warszawa (warszawa.wyborcza.pl); kontekst systemowy: Rzecznik Praw Obywatelskich i Najwyższa Izba Kontroli More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: The labour inspectorate may establish an employment relationship by decision — what it means for foreign nationals on civil-law contracts
item.description:
The Act of 11 March 2026 amending the Act on the National Labour Inspectorate and certain other acts (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473) empowers the regional labour inspector to establish, by decision, the existence of an employment relationship where a civil-law contract was concluded or work is in fact performed under the conditions of art. 22 § 1 Kodeksu pracy. A decision requires prior failure to comply with an order to remedy breaches. An appeal lies to the district court — the labour court — within one month of delivery. The act also introduces individual interpretations issued by the Chief Labour Inspector on whether a given legal relationship is an employment relationship; these bind PIP bodies. For foreign nationals working on a mandate contract or B2B this matters, because reclassification affects the basis for performing work, social insurance (ZUS) contributions and employee entitlements. The entry-into-force dates of individual provisions should be verified in the text of the act.
Source: Dziennik Ustaw 2026 poz. 473 (tekst ustawy za INFOR.pl) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Government plans to ban work under visa-free travel for citizens of Georgia, Colombia and Venezuela
item.description:
The Polish government plans to restrict the use of visa-free travel by citizens of Georgia, Colombia and Venezuela where entry to Poland or stay on its territory is connected with performing work. In practice, citizens of those three countries wishing to work in Poland would first have to obtain a national visa, and migration risk is assessed when one is issued. The measure takes the form of a regulation setting out a list of countries; the initiative came from the foreign ministry and was supported by MSWiA, justified by systemic use of visa-free travel to take up work outside the legal requirements. Note: as at publication this is a plan or draft — the entry-into-force date and the final list of countries should be verified at source. For employers it means planning recruitment from these countries earlier and allowing for visa waiting times.
Source: Raczkowski (PRO HR Immigration Update, lipiec 2026) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: MSWiA draft: a residence decision in 60 days and work without a permit — but only for citizens of selected countries
item.description:
The Ministry of the Interior and Administration (Ministerstwo Spraw Wewnetrznych i Administracji, MSWiA) has published a draft amendment to the Act on Foreigners intended to speed up residence proceedings initiated by citizens of selected countries, with a decision within 60 days. The draft also provides for work in Poland without a work permit for citizens of selected countries. The list of countries has not yet been officially indicated; the Raczkowski firm expects the beneficiaries to be nationals of Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Israel, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Taiwan, South Korea and Japan — this is an expert forecast, not the wording of the provision, and requires verification against the final text. Note: this is still a DRAFT and is not in force. The entry-into-force date and the final scope of countries are not settled and should be verified at source (legislative progress on the RCL and Sejm websites).

item.title: EU extends temporary protection for refugees from Ukraine to 4 March 2028 — with a new condition for men of conscription age
item.description:
On 30 July 2026 EU Member States completed the written procedure and formally agreed to extend temporary protection for refugees from Ukraine by another year, to 4 March 2028. A new condition was introduced at the same time: protection will not be granted to persons who have not fulfilled the military obligations provided for in Ukrainian law and for that reason have not obtained permission from the Ukrainian authorities to leave Ukraine (mobilisation in Ukraine covers men aged 25–60). The restriction does NOT apply to those already covered by temporary protection in the EU — only to first-time applicants. Proof of compliance may be, for example, a passport with an exit stamp from the Ukrainian authorities or a document on exemption from military service. About 4.4 million Ukrainians benefit from temporary protection in the EU. The measure enters into force the day after publication in the Official Journal of the EU. What this means for Poland: extension at EU level is the basis for extending Polish rules on UKR status — the specific Polish deadlines and procedure should be verified in the published legal acts. We also recall a separate Polish obligation: persons who obtained a PESEL UKR number without presenting a travel document must present it at the municipal office by 31 August 2026.
Source: Bankier.pl (za PAP) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549
